diagnosis.root_cause: The ONU transmitter is ageing: TX bias current has risen from approximately 11.6 mA to 15.2 mA while RX power remains broadly stable in the normal band and fibre distance is unchanged. TX optical power has also declined from about 2.4 dBm to 2.0 dBm.
evidence: The ONU is currently online and responding, with RX power around -23.95 dBm and TX power around 2.04 dBm, both within normal operating ranges.
RX telemetry remains broadly stable near -24 dBm and the distance stays constant at 241, so there is no evidence of fibre-path degradation or a distance change.
TX bias current rises steadily from roughly 11.6 mA to above 15 mA, exceeding the healthy 9.5-13.0 mA range.
TX power trends downward from roughly 2.4 dBm to 2.0 dBm while RX remains stable, matching laser degradation rather than fibre degradation.
The customer has six sessions in 24 hours, below the 8-session flapping threshold, and the optical trend is the primary discriminator.
All visible peers on EPON0/7 are online and the OLT, router, VLAN, RADIUS entry, and customer VLAN mapping are healthy, limiting the fault to this customer's ONU transmitter.

remediation.action: Replace the ONU or its optical transmitter, then verify TX power and bias current remain within healthy limits. Continue monitoring optical levels and session stability until replacement; do not replace shared PON infrastructure because all tested peers and the OLT are healthy.

ground_truth.root_cause: The ONU transmit laser is at end of life. Bias current has risen from 11.4 to 15.1 mA and, over the last two days, output power has begun to fall despite it, meaning compensation is now failing.
expected_reasoning: The customer reports progressive worsening, which fits both fibre degradation and laser degradation
RX sits at -23.9 dBm in the low-normal band and is noisier than the usual floor, but it is flat with no downward trend
TX bias current has climbed from 11.4 to 15.1 mA, well past the 13.0 mA ceiling
TX power held at 2.42 dBm while bias rose, then began falling to 2.05 dBm in the last two days
Falling output despite maximum bias means the laser can no longer compensate
Supply voltage has drifted from 3.45 to 3.36 V, consistent with a failing transmitter
Distance is constant, so there has been no change to the fibre path
Peers on EPON0/7 are normal, so shared infrastructure is not involved
Flat RX with collapsing TX is a transmitter fault, not path attenuation
distractors: RX in the low-normal band with extra noise invites a fibre degradation diagnosis
Steadily declining traffic fits either fault equally well
The complaint wording matches the fibre degradation pattern almost exactly
